page.definition_block: Upholsterers cover and restore upholstered furniture. Their work includes stripping old coverings from sofas, seats, and mattresses; repairing frames and springs; measuring and cutting fabric; sewing and adding padding; fastening materials with staple guns; and finishing edges. It is a skilled trade that combines frames, padding, and fabric into finished upholstered products.

responsibilities_block: Remove old upholstery, then inspect and repair frames, springs, and padding.
Measure from drawings, plan material layouts, and cut leather or fabric.
Sew fabric components and join the structures needed for covering.
Add padding, apply the covering, staple it in place, and stretch the fabric smooth.
Finish edges, install zippers and buttons, complete the product, and inspect quality.
Customize dimensions and styles for customers and collaborate on interior-furnishing design.
page.work_context_block: Most of the day is spent between the cutting table and sewing machine. You measure, mark, and plan layouts to reduce waste; cuts must be precise and seams straight. When adding padding and coverings, you need enough strength to pull the fabric smooth, fasten it staple by staple, and finish the edges. Custom jobs also require confirming dimensions and styles with customers and reworking the piece until they are satisfied.
